title: Memory-leak with HTTP3
body:
### I did this

Building with `-DUSE_NGHTTP3`, `-DCURLDEBUG` etc. And issuing these commands (in a .bat-file):
```
  set CURL_MEMDEBUG=c:\temp\memdebug.curl
  set CURL_DEBUG=http2,http3,setup
  set CURL_SSL_BACKEND=rustls
  curl.exe --http3 -v4oNUL https://www.google.com
  ...
  *   Trying 142.250.74.132:443...
  * QUIC cipher selection: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256:TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384:TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256:TLS_AES_128_CCM_SHA256
  *  CAfile: f:\MingW32\src\inet\curl\ca-bundle.pem  << !! leak at 3392?
    ...
  * Connected to www.google.com (142.250.74.132) port 443
  * ALPN: curl offers h2,http/1.1
  * rustls_connection wants us to write_tls.
  * Curl_socket_check: reading would block
  * Curl_socket_check: reading would block
  * Curl_socket_check: reading would block
  * Curl_socket_check: reading would block
  * Curl_socket_check: reading would block
  *  subjectAltName: host "www.google.com" matched cert's "*.google.com"
  * Verified certificate just fine
  * Connected to www.google.com (142.250.74.132) port 443
  * [SETUP] close
  * [SETUP] destroy
  * using HTTP/3
  * STATE: CONNECTING => PROTOCONNECT handle 0x26d5ae2a328; line 2144
  * STATE: PROTOCONNECT => DO handle 0x26d5ae2a328; line 2176
  * Server auth using Basic with user 'anonymous'
  * [HTTP/3] [0] OPENED stream for https://www.google.com/
  * [HTTP/3] [0] [:method: GET]
  * [HTTP/3] [0] [:scheme: https]
  * [HTTP/3] [0] [:authority: www.google.com]
  * [HTTP/3] [0] [:path: /]
  * [HTTP/3] [0] [authorization: Basic YW5vbnltb3VzOnlvdXJAZW1haWwuYWRkcmVzcw==]
   ...
```

shows some leaks from `perl tests/memanalyze.pl %CURL_MEMDEBUG%`:
```
  Leak detected: memory still allocated: 71 bytes
  At 1c572a9a4a8, there's 39 bytes.
   allocated by vtls/openssl.c:3392
  At 1c572a9aca8, there's 32 bytes.
   allocated by vtls/openssl.c:3381
  Open FILE handles left at:
  fopen() called at vtls/keylog.c:61
```

Strange to me that there are leaks in `vtls/openssl.c` when I did a `set CURL_SSL_BACKEND=rustls`.
Or is there some common code also used for RustTls?

But I'd assume `ossl_free_multi_ssl_backend_data()` should free these blocks. 
And the key-logfile should be closed via `ossl_cleanup()`. Seems it's called, but perhaps it's opened twice?


### I expected the following

No memory leaks.

### curl/libcurl version
